key_insight: Thinning freestanding BaTiO3 membranes suppresses visible cracking but shifts failure toward dense nanoscale wrinkling, with polymer support thickness further tuning wrinkle density.
engineering_relevance: The results provide thickness-selection guidelines for integrating freestanding ferroelectric oxide membranes into silicon-compatible low-power electronic and memory devices.
method: Release BaTiO3 membranes with varied oxide thickness (15 nm to 5 nm).
Adjust polymer support thickness during release.
Assess crack/wrinkle morphology and ferroelectric contrast with optical inspection and piezoresponse force microscopy.
evidence_signal: Abstract reports that reducing BaTiO3 thickness eliminates large-area cracks in analyzed regions, while 10 nm membranes show support-thickness-dependent wrinkle changes and time-evolving PFM contrast after release.
watch_item: Suppressing cracks does not guarantee stable device behavior, because ultrathin membranes may still develop dense wrinkling and time-dependent PFM signals influenced by morphology, screening, and strain relaxation.
paper_title: Thickness-dependent crack suppression and wrinkle formation in freestanding BaTiO3 membranes
